file_order_rationale: 8 ingest files ordered by their own header comments' declared promotion sequence (security_profile -> financial_facts -> quote_snapshot -> corporate_actions -> sdi_disclosure -> directorate -> ownership -> related_warrants), followed by the 8 entitlement files in the same per-domain order. Each file is independently transactional (its own BEGIN...COMMIT plus an internal readback DO block), so a later file's failure does not roll back an earlier file's already-committed and already-verified promotion.
rls_write_path: Confirmed by running this exact 16-file, 16-order packet against netquity_serving_writer_staging in a local scratch Postgres seeded with the real netquity mirror: all 16 files (deploy/ingest/*.sql files 1-8, then deploy/account/*-entitlement-staging.sql files 9-16) complete successfully end to end in one run. aiphabee_governance.data_entitlement and aiphabee_governance.workspace_entitlement both have force row level security; deploy/database/roles/netquity-serving-writer-staging.sql adds four role-targeted policies (netquity_serving_writer_entitlement_select, netquity_serving_writer_entitlement_insert, netquity_serving_writer_entitlement_update, netquity_serving_writer_workspace_entitlement_insert, each TO netquity_serving_writer_staging only) so PostgreSQL no longer denies those two tables' SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE commands under FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY's zero-policy default-deny. The SELECT policy is required because INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (data_entitlement's shape) needs SELECT-policy visibility into the row identity even when nothing actually conflicts, which the pre-existing member-scoped SELECT policy cannot supply for a brand-new entitlement_id. netquity_serving_writer_staging still has no BYPASSRLS; the pre-existing member-scoped SELECT policies (data_entitlement_member_read, workspace_entitlement_member_read) are untouched, and the four new policies apply to no other role.
